gloss: tent; a household; pitch a tent
summary: אֹהֶל is a tent: the dwelling of curtains, cords and pegs that the fathers pitched and struck as they moved (Gen 12:8; Isa 33:20), and so a man’s home and household, whatever it was built of: “every man to his tents, Israel” (1Ki 12:16), “the tent of Joseph” set beside the tribe of Ephraim (Psa 78:67). Above all it is the tent Yahweh had made for himself in Israel’s midst, the אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד, “tent of meeting”, where he met and spoke with Moses and at whose entrance the congregation gathered at the trumpets’ call (Exo 29:42; Num 10:3). The verb אָהַל, made from the noun, is to pitch or move one’s tent. Ugaritic and Jewish Aramaic have the word for “tent”, while Arabic ʾahl, Phoenician and Sabaean ʾhl mean the people of a house: family, clan.

words.gloss: tent; home, household; Yahweh’s tent, the tent of meeting

senses.definition: A dwelling of curtains stretched on poles and held by cords and pegs, pitched and taken down as its people moved: the home of those who keep flocks and herds, of the fathers in the land, of armies in the field.

evidence.note: Jabal was the father of יֹשֵׁב אֹהֶל וּמִקְנֶה, those who dwell in tents and have livestock.
Abram “stretched out his tent” (וַיֵּט אָהֳלֹה) between Bethel and Ai and built an altar there.
He went by his stages back to the place where his tent had been at the beginning.
Lot had flocks, herds and tents.
Yahweh appeared to Abraham as he sat at the opening of the tent in the heat of the day.
Isaac brought Rebekah into the tent of Sarah his mother.
Jacob a quiet man, יֹשֵׁב אֹהָלִים, set against Esau the man of the field.
Laban searched the tents of Jacob, Leah and the two maidservants, and Rachel’s tent.
Jerusalem “a tent that will not be moved; its pegs will never be pulled up, and none of its cords broken”: what a tent is made of and how it is struck.
“My tent is plundered and all my cords are snapped … none to stretch out my tent any more and to set up my curtains.”
Jael took a tent peg (יְתַד הָאֹהֶל) and a hammer.
“Blessed above women in the tent.”
The Rechabites were to build no house, sow no seed, plant no vineyard, “but in tents you shall dwell all your days … where you sojourn”.
“Black, but lovely, like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon.”
“I dwell among the tents of Kedar.”
The Arameans fled in the twilight and left their tents, horses and donkeys, the camp as it was.
Midian came up with their livestock and their tents, like locusts.
The law when a man dies in a tent: all who come into the tent and all in it are unclean seven days.
Hezekiah: “My dwelling is pulled up and removed from me like a shepherd’s tent; like a weaver I have rolled up my life”: a tent struck, as a picture of dying.
The king of the north “will plant the tents of his palace” between the seas and the glorious holy mountain.
Abraham dwelt in tents (ἐν σκηναῖς) with Isaac and Jacob, sojourning in the land of promise as in a foreign land.

senses.gloss: the heavens spread as a tent
senses.definition: Yahweh stretching out the heavens as a man stretches a tent to live in, and setting in them a tent for the sun.

evidence.note: He “stretches out the heavens like a curtain and spreads them like a tent to dwell in”.
“In them he has set a tent for the sun.”
Zion told to enlarge the place of her tent, stretch out her curtains and lengthen her cords, for her children will be many.

senses.definition: Where a man lives and those who live with him, whatever the dwelling is built of: to go “to one’s tents” is to go home, and “the tents of” a people are that people, set beside house, tribe and nation.

evidence.note: “To your tents, Israel! Now see to your own house, David!” Israel went to its tents: tent set against David’s house, both meaning household and allegiance.
“We have no portion in David … every man to his tents, Israel.”
After the dedication of the house of Yahweh the people went to their tents, glad of heart: Israel settled in the land, going home.
Israel dwelt in their tents as before, once delivered from Aram.
After the Passover eaten at the place Yahweh chooses, “in the morning you shall turn and go to your tents”.
Gideon sent every man of Israel to his tents.
Israel was struck and fled, every man to his tents.
David: “I will not enter the tent of my house”: אֹהֶל בֵּיתִי, the tent that is his house.
“The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish”: tent set parallel to house.
“You will know that your tent is at peace, and you will visit your habitation (נָוְךָ) and miss nothing.”
מְתֵי אָהֳלִי, “the men of my tent”: Job’s household.
“When the counsel of God was over my tent.”
The wicked man is torn from his tent, his trust, and marched to the king of terrors.
“Put unrighteousness far from your tents.”
“The voice of rejoicing and salvation is in the tents of the righteous.”
Better a doorkeeper in the house of my God than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.
“He rejected the tent of Joseph, and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim”: tent parallel to tribe.
He struck the firstborn in Egypt, the first of their strength in the tents of Ham.
“The tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites”: peoples named by their tents.
The tents of Cushan, parallel to the curtains of the land of Midian.
“May he dwell in the tents of Shem.”
“How good are your tents, Jacob, your dwellings, Israel.”
“I will turn the captivity of the tents of Jacob and have compassion on his dwellings, and the city will be built on its mound.”
Yahweh will save the tents of Judah first.
Yahweh will cut off from the tents of Jacob the man who does this.
God will pluck you out of the tent and root you out of the land of the living.

senses.gloss: Yahweh’s tent: the tent of meeting
senses.definition: The tent Yahweh had Israel make for him in the wilderness, spread over the מִשְׁכָּן, where he met his people and spoke with Moses, at whose entrance offerings were brought and the congregation gathered; called אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד “tent of meeting” and אֹהֶל הָעֵדֻת “tent of the testimony”; after it, the tent David pitched for the ark, and the name carried over to the house that replaced it.

evidence.note: The continual burnt offering at the entrance of the אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד before Yahweh, “where I will meet with you, to speak to you there” (אִוָּעֵד, the verb of מוֹעֵד).
“I will make holy the tent of meeting and the altar.”
Curtains of goats’ hair “for a tent over the מִשְׁכָּן”: the tent is the covering spread over the dwelling.
Moses spread the tent over the מִשְׁכָּן and put the covering of the tent on it.
The cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of Yahweh filled the מִשְׁכָּן.
Moses pitched the tent outside the camp and called it אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד; everyone who sought Yahweh went out to it.
The pillar of cloud came down and stood at the entrance of the tent, and spoke with Moses.
Yahweh spoke to Moses face to face; Joshua did not depart from the tent.
When Moses went into the tent of meeting he heard the voice speaking to him from above the כַּפֹּרֶת between the cherubim.
Yahweh called to Moses and spoke to him from the tent of meeting.
When both silver trumpets are blown, all the congregation gathers (וְנוֹעֲדוּ) to Moses at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Aaron and his sons wear the linen breeches when they come into the tent of meeting, lest they bear iniquity and die.
On the day the מִשְׁכָּן was set up the cloud covered it, “the tent of the testimony”.
Moses went into the tent of the testimony, and Aaron’s rod had budded.
The tax Moses laid on Israel “for the tent of the testimony”.
“I have not dwelt in a house … but have been walking in a tent and in a מִשְׁכָּן”: tent set against house.
He forsook the מִשְׁכָּן of Shiloh, the tent he had set among men.
The ark set in its place inside the tent David had pitched for it.
Zadok took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon.
Joab fled to the tent of Yahweh and took hold of the horns of the altar.
The ark, the tent of meeting and its holy vessels brought up into Solomon’s house.
Gatekeepers of “the house of Yahweh, the house of the tent”.
In the house Ezekiel is shown, the width of the הֵיכָל is “the width of the tent”.
He poured out his fury like fire on the tent of the daughter of Zion.
A throne established in kindness, and one sitting on it in truth “in the tent of David”, judging and seeking justice.
“Our fathers had the tent of the testimony (ἡ σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου) in the wilderness, made as he had commanded Moses.”
Moses was warned, when about to finish the tent, to make all according to the pattern shown him on the mountain.

senses.definition: In the Psalms, to dwell in Yahweh’s tent is to live as his guest under his protection.

evidence.note: “Yahweh, who will sojourn in your tent? Who will dwell on your holy mountain?”
“Let me sojourn in your tent for ever; let me take refuge in the hiding place of your wings.”
He hides me in his סֻכָּה in the day of trouble, in the secret place of his tent.
“I will offer in his tent sacrifices of shouting.”

evidence.locator: אֹהֶל → σκηνή ×218 of 346 (lemma count, MACULA alignment); Gen.12.8, Exo.33.7, Num.10.3, Isa.40.22, Hos.12.10 (Hebrew numbering)

evidence.note: Christ a minister of the holy places and of the true tent, which the Lord pitched, not man.
Through the greater and more perfect tent, not made with hands.
Abraham dwelt in tents with Isaac and Jacob.
The temple of the tent of the testimony in heaven was opened.
“The tent of God is with men, and he will dwell (σκηνώσει) with them.”

evidence.locator: אֹהֶל → σκήνωμα ×15 (lemma count); 1Sa.4.10, 1Ki.2.28, Psa.19.5, Psa.78.60, Psa.78.67, Psa.132.3

evidence.note: “As long as I am in this tent (σκηνώματι).”
“The putting off of my tent comes quickly.”

parallels.note: Tent beside dwelling, of Israel’s homes and of Yahweh’s; in the tabernacle the אֹהֶל is the covering spread over the מִשְׁכָּן.
Tent and house set side by side as a man’s home.
Tent beside habitation, a settled abode.
The curtains a tent is made of.
Yahweh’s booth beside his tent as a hiding place.
The tent of Joseph beside the tribe of Ephraim: a tent is a family line.

opposites.note: A tent set against a built house: the sojourner’s dwelling against the settled one.

phrases.gloss: tent of meeting, where Yahweh meets his people
every man to his tents: home, disbanding

words.summary: A verb made from the noun, three times: to live as a tent-dweller, moving one’s tent from place to place.

senses.definition: Take up one’s tent and pitch it in a new place, living as a tent-dweller.

evidence.note: Abram dwelt in the land of Canaan, Lot in the cities of the plain, “and he tented as far as Sodom”.
Abram moved his tent and came and dwelt by the oaks of Mamre, and built an altar to Yahweh there.

senses.definition: Set up a tent to stay, said of a nomad; the form יַהֵל is contracted.

evidence.note: Babylon will never be inhabited; “no Arab will pitch his tent there, and no shepherds make their flocks lie down there”.

words.summary: Once, in the hiphil, of the moon not shining in God’s eyes. Its sense is that of הָלַל “shine” (Isa 13:10; Job 31:26), whose forms יָהֵל and בְּהִלּוֹ it resembles, and the link to “tent” is not known; it may be a by-form of that verb. No cognate of אהל shares it.

senses.definition: Of the moon: give out its light, be bright; parallel to the stars’ being pure.

evidence.note: “Behold, even the moon does not shine (יַאֲהִיל), and the stars are not pure in his eyes.”
Compare הָלַל: the stars “will not let their light shine” (לֹא יָהֵלּוּ אוֹרָם).
Compare הָלַל: “if I looked at the light when it shone (יָהֵל), or the moon moving in splendour”.

words.summary: Four times, in the plural (אֲהָלִים, אֲהָלוֹת), a fragrant wood or tree named with myrrh and spices. It is most likely the name of a foreign tree, and no link to the root’s “tent” is known; it shares only the spelling. Balaam plays on the two: “how good are your tents (אֹהָלֶיךָ) … like aloes (כַּאֲהָלִים) Yahweh has planted” (Num 24:5–6).

senses.definition: A tree whose wood gives a sweet scent, used with myrrh and cinnamon to perfume garments and a bed, and growing like a tree Yahweh has planted.

evidence.note: “Myrrh and aloes and cassia are all your garments.”
“I have sprinkled my bed with myrrh, aloes and cinnamon.”
Among the spices of the garden: “myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices”.
“Like aloes that Yahweh has planted, like cedars beside the waters”: a tree, beside the cedars.
Nicodemus brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes (ἀλόης), about a hundred pounds, for Jesus’ burial: the pair of Psa 45:9 and Sng 4:14.
In the Septuagint only at Song 4:14 in Codex Sinaiticus, for אֲהָלִים; New Testament John 19:39.

cognates.note: The same word as Hebrew אֹהֶל, with the same meaning, in the language of Ugarit; Segert sets it beside Hebrew ʾōhel and Arabic ʾahl.
Jewish Aramaic: a tent, and the sheet spread as its cover, “he breaks the tent up” by taking off part of its cover; Targum Jonathan at Num 12:12.

evidence.note: Targ. Y. Num. 12:12; Bets. 30b; Sabb. 137b.

cognates.gloss: the people of a house or tent, family, kin; (verb) be peopled, inhabited; take a wife
cognates.note: Lane’s sources give أَهْل as “the people of a house or dwelling, and of a town or village … and the family of a man”, and أَهْلُ البَيْتِ as “the inhabitants or family of the house or tent”; the verb أَهَلَ is “it (a place) was peopled, inhabited” and “he married”. Arabic keeps the household that a Hebrew tent stands for (1Ki 12:16; Psa 78:67), not the tent itself.
In Phoenician names: ʾhlbʿl “Baal is my family”, ʾhlmlk “Milk is my family”. Krahmalkov sets it beside Hebrew ʾohel and Arabic ʾahl.
Sabaean (Old South Arabian): “the people of the coastland and the highland”, “his family and their land”, “the clan of …”; Biella compares Arabic ʾahl.

Set with ʾhl under one Proto-Semitic root by Anderson and Moser, as a settled place where a people lives. Akkadian ālu shows no h, and the link rests on the reconstruction, so it is recorded as possible, on the household sense.

doctrine.statement: Yahweh had a tent made for himself in Israel’s midst and named it the tent of meeting, “where I will meet with you, to speak to you there” (Exo 29:42); when it was set up the cloud covered it and his glory filled the dwelling (Exo 40:34–35), and from it he spoke to Moses face to face (Exo 33:9–11; Num 7:89). He told David that he had not dwelt in a house but had walked in a tent (2Sa 7:6). Hebrews calls that tent a copy and shadow made to the pattern shown on the mountain, and Christ the minister of “the true tent, which the Lord pitched, not man”, who entered through “the greater and more perfect tent, not made with hands” (Heb 8:2, 5; 9:11). John writes that the word became flesh and tented (ἐσκήνωσεν) among us, “and we beheld his glory” (John 1:14), and the end of Revelation is “the tent of God is with men, and he will tent with them” (Rev 21:3). From the verses: the tent was where God met man and showed his glory in Israel; that meeting place is found in Jesus, in whose flesh God’s glory was seen, and it ends with God dwelling with his people on the earth.

Abraham pitched his tent in the land and built altars there (Gen 12:8; 13:18), and lived in tents with Isaac and Jacob, “heirs with him of the same promise”, sojourning in the land of promise as in a foreign land, for he looked for the city that has foundations (Heb 11:9–10). Stephen says God gave him no inheritance in it, not even a foot’s length, yet promised to give it to him and to his seed after him (Act 7:5); Hebrews says these all died in faith, not having received the promises, and will not be made perfect apart from us (Heb 11:13, 39–40). From the verses: the fathers’ tents mark men who were promised the land and did not yet own it; the promise stands, to be received by them with all the faithful together, which is at the resurrection.

Hezekiah, sick to death, says “my dwelling is pulled up and removed from me like a shepherd’s tent; like a weaver I have rolled up my life” (Isa 38:12), and the Psalm says God will pluck the wicked out of the tent and root him out of the land of the living (Psa 52:7). Paul calls the body “our earthly house of this tent”, which is taken down, and says that in this tent we groan, not wishing to be unclothed but clothed upon, “that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life” (2Co 5:1, 4); Peter calls his body “this tent”, soon to be put off (2Pe 1:13–14). From the verses: a man’s life is a tent pitched for a time and struck at death; the hope set out is not a part of him that lives on unhoused, but being clothed with a dwelling from God, the mortal swallowed up by life.

Lev 23 has Israel live in סֻכֹּת seven days “so that your generations may know that I made the sons of Israel dwell in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt” (Lev 23:42–43). Hosea, to an Israel grown rich in the land, has Yahweh say: “I am Yahweh your God from the land of Egypt; I will yet make you dwell in tents as in the days of the appointed feast” (Hos 12:10), and he will lead her into the wilderness and speak to her heart, and she will answer “as in the day she came up from the land of Egypt” (Hos 2:16–17). From the verses: the feast keeps in memory the tents of the exodus, and Hosea sets those tents in Israel’s future: Yahweh will bring his people back through a wilderness to himself, as he did when he brought them out of Egypt.

note: Drafted 2026-11-13 for Num 10 (Num 10:3, the trumpets gathering the congregation to the entrance of the tent of meeting). Root key אהל as the corpus keys it. Words: אֹהֶל (a.bl.ab), the denominative verb אָהַל (a.bl.ac; qal Gen 13:12, 18, piel Isa 13:20 יַהֵל), hiphil אָהַל “shine” (a.bm.aa, Job 25:5) and אֲהָלִים/אֲהָלוֹת “aloes” (a.bn.aa). a.bl.aa is BDB’s root heading with no tokens. Left out as names: Aaron (a.bn.ab; names/aaron.json, whose letters do not contain ל, so its place here is only BDB’s filing), and the names formed from אֹהֶל: Oholah (a.bl.ad, Ezk 23), Oholibah (a.bl.af, Ezk 23), Oholiab (a.bl.ae, Exo 31:6) and Oholibamah (a.bl.ag, Gen 36), which have no name entries yet. “Shine” is kept with a summary saying its link is not known; it may belong with הלל. “Aloes” is kept the same way; a foreign origin for the tree name is likely but no Semitic or Indian dictionary was checked, so it is not recorded as a loan. Open questions: (1) whether Arabic ʾahl, Phoenician and Sabaean ʾhl (family, people) are the same word as “tent” or only kin to the household sense; they are named on the household sense, and Ugaritic and Aramaic “tent” on the tent senses. (2) Doctrine “tents-again” reads Hos 12:10 as a promise tied to the feast of booths; it could also be read as a threat of exile; check the framing. (3) Doctrine “heirs-in-tents” states the land promise received at the resurrection from Heb 11:39–40. Leads not followed: Syriac (Wiktionary gives ܝܗܠܐ yahlā; SEDRA has no word of this root in the Peshitta, and Payne Smith was not checked); Ge’ez not found; Akkadian ālu recorded only as possible.
